narrative: 在一段时间内，观众就是角色本身。《湖中女》（Lady in the Lake）就是这样讲述一个侦探故事。
《硬核亨利》（Hardcore Henry）把它用作一具动作中的身体；《遁入虚无》（Enter the Void）则让镜头始终停留在一个意识之中，即便如此，它依然要穿行于各个房间之间。
手、方向盘、一把枪、画面边缘被推开的一扇门：这些细节表明看的人是一个具体的人，而不是隐形的旁观者。主观镜头（Point of View）可以只是切入他们所看到内容的一个镜头，画面中不带任何身体归属的痕迹。
第一人称视角始终让“看的人”作为一个可感知的身体存在。物体视角（Object POV）则是把摄影机绑定在一件道具上。
斯诺里康（SnorriCam）是从胸前拍摄人物自己的脸，归属关系正好相反。
how: 把摄影机绑定在角色的头部或上胸位置，使用接近人眼的视野（球面镜头大约24mm到35mm，除非剧情本身需要，否则不要用运动相机式的超广角）。允许手、画面极边缘的肩膀或一件工具入镜。
呼吸和脚步造成的镜头晃动，幅度要符合一个真实身体的运动，不要过度。除非透过镜子或玻璃，否则不要露出“看的人”的脸。
提示词：first-person camera as [Subject] would see, hands entering frame, breath, a body that owns the lens.
when: 当观众必须成为角色本人、而不只是短暂地代入他们的视角时使用。具体场景：在湿滑的天桥上奔跑，戴手套的手拍在栏杆上，寒气中的呼吸声，看不到奔跑者的脸。
不要把它用在双人对峙争吵的场景里，那样会让观众跟丢另一方。
vs: 主观镜头（Point of View）是所见世界的一个光学切片，通常是在一个“看”的镜头之后插入的画面，画面中不允许出现看的人的身体。物体视角（Object POV）则是一颗球、一颗子弹、一部手机、一辆车的视角。
过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）让我们待在某个仍能被看见的人身后。打破第四面墙（Fourth Wall）则是角色转过来看我们。
斯诺里康（SnorriCam）把摄影机固定在躯干上，死死盯着人物自己的脸，而周围的世界在画面中滑动。
examples_film: 《硬核亨利》（Hardcore Henry）始终把身体留在镜头中：手、武器、撞击。《遁入虚无》（Enter the Void）则在肉身消逝之后，仍以一条移动的第一人称路径，让意识穿行于空间之中。
《湖中女》（Lady in the Lake, 1947）尝试用第一人称贯穿整部侦探片，其他角色直接对着镜头说话，把它当作马洛（Marlowe）本人。可以把这些处理方式当作“具身化”的语法来借鉴。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的是一个干净的主观镜头（Point of View）画面（没有手入镜），或是演员身后的跟随镜头（Follow Shot）。识别标志：只拍到后脑勺，或是一个完全没有身体感的房间固定镜头。
修正方法：让手或工具入镜，运动要像走路或转头的动作，“看的人”的脸始终不出现。如果摄影机是固定在车头上、画面里带着车身的铬饰，那你要的其实是物体视角（Object POV）。

faq.q: 电影中的第一人称镜头是什么？
faq.a: 第一人称让摄影机成为角色的身体：我们像他们一样去看，手、呼吸或工具会进入画面。这是一种持续的具身体验，而不只是短暂的一瞥。

faq.q: 第一人称视角与主观镜头（POV）的区别
faq.a: 主观镜头（POV）是角色所看到的画面，通常是一个不带身体痕迹的单独插入镜头。第一人称视角则会在一段时间内持续保留镜头的身体归属：手、移动、呼吸。

faq.q: 什么时候应该使用第一人称视角？
faq.a: 当观众需要在一段动作或感知过程中“占据”一具身体时使用。不要把它用在普通的正反打对话场景中。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写第一人称视角的提示词？
faq.a: 可以这样写：First-person camera as [Subject] would see, hands entering frame, breath, a body that owns the lens. 拍视频时，运动方式要与角色的移动一致，工具出现在画面边缘，不露出“看的人”的脸。

narrative: The audience is the character for a stretch of time. Lady in the Lake tries to tell a detective story this way.
Hardcore Henry runs it as an action body. Enter the Void keeps the camera inside a consciousness that still has a path through rooms.

Hands, a steering wheel, a gun, a door handled at the edge: those are the tells that a person, not an invisible observer, is looking. A Point of View shot can be one cut of what they see, clean of the owner.
First-person keeps the owner as a felt body. Object POV parents the camera to a prop instead.
SnorriCam looks at their face from their chest, which is the opposite ownership.
how: Parent the camera to the character's head or upper chest with a human field of view (roughly 24mm to 35mm spherical, not a tiny action-cam unless that is diegetic). Allow hands, shoulders at the extreme edge, or a tool to enter.
Add breath and footfall as camera motion only as much as a body would. Do not show the owner's face except in glass.
Prompt: first-person camera as [Subject] would see, hands entering frame, breath, a body that owns the lens.
when: Use it when the audience must be the character, not merely glance as them. Concrete beat: running a wet overpass, gloved hands hitting the rail, breath in the cold, no face of the runner.
Do not use it for a two-shot argument; you will lose the listener.
vs: Point of View is the optical slice of the seen world, often an insert after a look, owner body forbidden. Object POV is a ball, a bullet, a phone, a vehicle.
Over-the-Shoulder Coverage keeps us behind someone we can still see. Fourth Wall has them look at us.
SnorriCam bolts the camera to the torso and stares at their face while the world slides.
examples_film: Hardcore Henry keeps the body in the lens: hands, weapons, impacts. Enter the Void rides a consciousness through space after the body is gone, still as a moving first-person path.
Lady in the Lake (1947) attempts extended first-person detective storytelling, other characters addressing the lens as Marlowe. Use those as embodiment grammar.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a clean Point of View plate (no hands) or a Follow Shot behind the actor. Tell: a back of a head, or a perfectly disembodied lock-off of a room.
Fix: hands or a tool in frame, motion as a walk or a turn of the head, owner invisible as a face. If the camera is bolted to a car hood with chrome in frame, you wanted Object POV.

faq.q: What is first-person camera in film?
faq.a: First-person makes the camera a character's body: we see as they see, with hands, breath, or tools entering the frame. It is continuous embodiment, not only a glance.
A POV shot is what they see, often a single insert with no owner body. First-person keeps a body owning the lens over time: hands, locomotion, breath.
Use it when the audience should inhabit a body for a passage of action or perception. Do not use it for ordinary reverse-shot dialogue.

faq.q: How do I prompt first-person for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: First-person camera as [Subject] would see, hands entering frame, breath, a body that owns the lens. For video, move as they move, tools at the edges, no owner's face.
